title: Dungeon Delicacies
author: DevNeroTheDev
selftext:
I always wanted to make a game that was like some anime that I really liked, like Delicious in Dungeon. So I made this single player dungeon exploration, crafting and cooking game with the help of AI. I used Claude for the code, making it in React as HTML5 game, and for the artwork I used my own art as a base then used Gemini to make variations for monsters, food, items etc. I feel I should still adjust the UI a bit more it kinda looks too simple. Hope you guys give it a try and let me know what you think. It's a Web PC game, not optimized for phones, and it's free to play, no ads, no purchases.

https://nerothearchangel.itch.io/dungeon-delicacies

comments.author: UnscriptedTheater
comments.body:
I played for just a few minutes. Feedback:

Cooking tab:  
I couldn't immediately tell that it was telling me how much of each ingredient is required. It would be helpful to note that, along with how many of the ingredient I have so I can see quickly without having to look at inventory.  
Ex:   
Grilled Rat  
Req: Rat Meat x2 | You have: Rat Meat x6

Dungeon tab:  
Add hover text to each of the items in quick meals so you can see the benefits they provide.

Bestiary tab:  
This would be cool if you only saw the stats for each enemy after you've defeated them. I get the feeling that's what you're going for here!

Final thoughts:  
First, this is only one person's feedback and the player isn't always right! But... I feel like you have the beginnings of what could be a neat idle game here. The different attacks are just levers to manage HP/Mana and enemy HP, right? What if there was just a "Battle" button that you could activate that auto-battles monsters on a regular interval and then allows you to do the fun stuff (cooking, crafting, etc). Again, just one player's thoughts! I think you have a good base and look forward to seeing what you do with it!

replies.author: DevNeroTheDev
replies.body:
First thank you for playing and for the feedback. 

1. Game does tell the player how much is needed to cook each meal. Also it uses green color to signify when there is enough. All items are in the inventory. You also only get 1x drop per monster killed. 

2. Kitchen provides info on all meals and what they do, players can alway switch to a different tab to check other items even mid fight.

3. Beastiary is for complete info on all monsters so that player can know what to expect on each floor. 

4. Skills are to help deal with stronger monsters on higher floors. And to add variety to the combat. 

I didn't want to implement auto battle system because it's very boring and overused. It's not engaging, especially for a clicker type game. This game is not for AFK play. It's to actively engage with the content. It autosaves every 5 seconds so the player can always come back and resume where they left off. 

Current combat system forces the player not to mindlessly click or use auto clickers because they will die without cooking enough of food, and without proper gear. Death sends you back to floor 1, makes you lose half of the food you had and decent chunk of gold. It also was made so that players once they level up won't get exp and gold on lower levels. So grinding same levels only works for early game. 

Again, thank you so much for taking the time and test and give me a valuable feedback. I hope my points explain the game better. Maybe I should make a tutorial in game explaining things better. I made this with assumption that people who play these types of clicker games already know how everything works.

comments.author: SproutsJeremy
comments.body:
It’s a really good start for a nice mobile/pc game app. Kudos to you, it definitely looks great. 

I was gonna mention some issues but it seems like this is supposed to be an idle clicker rather than an rpg. As the other guy said, you need more qol features like an indication of how many ingredients you have, and a game over screen. Also, every floor seems to have enemies that deal the same damage to you and there is no death screen/mechanics. 

But you could probably release this as is and get some people interested in it.

replies.author: DevNeroTheDev
replies.body:
Thank you for playing and sharing your opinion. As I mentioned game already has 2 indicators for the amount of item needed for something, numeric and color, plus all items are also found in inventory so I didn't want to spam same numbers everywhere, it would be redunant. 

If you go into bestiary you can see the amount of base dmg every monster does. This is also exponentially increased based on players lvl. For example if you spammed floors 1 and 2 and you're lvl 10 when you go to the floor 3 and above they will do more than their base dmg. 

You are right about adding the death screen, currently you get sent to floor1 and there is a notification that you died, would be better to have death screen. I'll add that ASAP.  Thanks again.

replies.author: SproutsJeremy
replies.body:
Oh okay well tbh the death screen was all that was necessary then. Everything else is good. 

I guess from here it’s mostly ready for release outside of some qol features you may want to add. And ofc content would be necessary too. 

A huge reason I love idle clickers is also because I get to buy houses, planes, boats, jets, which keeps me wanting more. I can see the next cool plane or house and I want to get it bad. So I’ll spend a half an hour just clicking till I get to buy it. Especially between coding or work. 

Passive income is definitely huge too. I like being able to buy property and rent it for passive income or just earn money from investing in businesses. 

From here it was probably already in your plans, but adding more and cooler enemies would definitely be cool. Adding cool medieval properties from a shack to a castle and collecting and storing pets and cool servants would be nice too. But for now after the death screen is set you’re pretty much straight

replies.author: DevNeroTheDev
replies.body: None of those are the features that go with this game unfortunately. No pets, castles, or buying property. The game is based off of 2 things cooking delicious food and exploring the dungeon. There are already 60 unique monsters in game, and 3 difficulty levels. It takes more than 40h to beat the game all difficulties and unlock all achievements. This is more of an active clicker not so much idle.
